title: Thirteen years
hookLine: the yaksha's questions, a brother chosen for fairness, the year in hiding
carry: dharma is fair even when it costs you
last: KRISHNA ANSWERS THE ONE WHO CALLS.

lines: CALLED BACK FOR ONE MORE THROW.
cards: You'd think, after all that, the Pandavas would never touch dice again. Freed by Draupadi's wishes, they head home, and they're called back. One more game, one throw.

The loser goes into the forest for twelve years, then spends a thirteenth year in hiding, somewhere in the world, undiscovered. If anyone recognizes them that year, they start all over again. Yudhishthira plays.
Yudhishthira loses. And five royal brothers and a queen walk into the forest with nothing.

teach.h: THE YAKSHA'S QUESTIONS AT THE LAKE.
teach.b: The twelve forest years fill a huge part of the Mahabharata: sages, pilgrimages, stories inside stories.

Near the end of them, the brothers, desperately thirsty, find a lake guarded by a spirit, a yaksha, who says: answer my questions before you drink. One by one, four brothers drink anyway and fall dead.
Yudhishthira stops and answers. The questions come fast. What is the greatest wonder in the world?
His answer, roughly: every day people die all around us, and the rest of us live as if we never will. He answers so well that the yaksha offers him a gift: one of your brothers may live. Choose.
Bhima, the strongest? Arjuna, the great archer, the one you'll need in a war?

teach.h: HE CHOOSES THE OTHER MOTHER'S SON.
teach.b: Yudhishthira chooses Nakula, one of the twins. Why him? Because the twins had a different mother, Madri.
Yudhishthira's own mother, Kunti, still has a living son: him. Let Madri have one too.

The yaksha is so moved that he gives all four back, and reveals who he really is: Dharma himself, the god of dharma and Yudhishthira's own father, testing his son. That's the teaching under the scene.
Dharma isn't only being right. It's being fair, even to the other side of the family, even when it costs you your best warrior.

teach.h: THE YEAR IN HIDING AT VIRATA'S COURT.

teach.b: They hide at the court of a king called Virata, each as the last thing you'd expect: Yudhishthira as the king's dice companion, mighty Bhima as a cook, Arjuna as Brihannala, a dance teacher, and Draupadi as a maid to the queen.
The year runs out, and they're not caught.

how: The Yaksha's questions to Yudhishthira are often retold and taught as a dialogue on dharma, and the Virata Parva, the book of the year in hiding, is traditionally recited in some regions to pray for rain.

games.q: you're Yudhishthira. the yaksha says one brother may live. Bhima's the strongest, Arjuna your best archer. who do you choose?
o: Arjuna. you'll need him in a war.
games.why: he chooses Nakula, so Madri has a living son just as Kunti does. the yaksha, Dharma himself, gives all four back.

practice: Think of a split you're part of: two sides of a family, two friends, two groups at work. Picture someone on the other side who stands to lose something too, the one who'll be hurt if it all stays broken.
Ask Yudhishthira's question: what would be fair to them, not only to me? If you pray, pray for them by name. Don't decide anything yet; just let their side be real.

wordCard.voice: Thirteen years. Twelve in the forest, and one in hiding, in plain sight, at a king's court.

orig.note: Sanskrit: ajnata (unknown) + vasa (dwelling). Living unrecognized: the year in hiding.
